rules.coverage_text: All residential rental properties in Berkeley.

key_values.name: maximum_screening_fee
key_values.text: The maximum tenant screening fee for 2026 is $68.96

rules.quote:
The maximum tenant screening fee for 2026 is
$68.96
rules.requirement: Landlords may not charge a prospective tenant a screening fee exceeding $68.96 in 2026.
rules.title: Maximum Tenant Screening Fee

rules.coverage_text: All residential rental properties in Berkeley.

key_values.name: credit_report_delivery_deadline
key_values.text: Prospective tenants should expect to receive a copy of their credit report within 7 days of receipt by the landlord

rules.quote: Landlords may use screening fees to obtain information about a prospective tenant like a consumer credit report. Prospective tenants should expect to receive a copy of their credit report within 7 days of receipt by the landlord, a receipt for the fee paid and an itemized list of any out-of-pocket expenses and time spent by the landlord on the screening, and a refund of any unused portion of the fee.
rules.requirement: When a landlord charges a screening fee, the prospective tenant must receive a copy of their credit report within 7 days of the landlord's receipt, a receipt for the fee paid, an itemized list of out-of-pocket expenses and time spent by the landlord, and a refund of any unused portion of the fee.
rules.title: Screening Fee Disclosures and Refunds

rules.coverage_text: All residential rental properties in Berkeley.
rules.quote: If the tenant provides a reusable screening report, the landlord must use it.
rules.requirement: Landlords must accept and use a reusable screening report provided by a prospective tenant instead of charging a new screening fee.
rules.title: Reusable Screening Report Requirement

rules.coverage_text: All residential rental properties in Berkeley.
rules.quote: The landlord cannot charge a prospective tenant a screening fee if no rental unit is actually available.
rules.requirement: Landlords may not charge a screening fee to a prospective tenant when no rental unit is actually available.
rules.title: Prohibition on Screening Fees When No Unit Available

rules.coverage_text: All residential rental properties in Berkeley.
rules.quote: The landlord must also return a screening fee to any applicant not selected, or have a policy under which they: (1) review applications in the order received and the first qualified applicant gets the unit, and (2) do not charge a screening fee to any applicant not considered.
rules.requirement: Landlords must either refund screening fees to applicants not selected, or adopt a policy of reviewing applications in order received and charging screening fees only to the first qualified applicant.
rules.title: Screening Fee Refund or First-Qualified Applicant Policy

rules.coverage_text: All residential rental properties in Berkeley.
rules.quote: When an owner or the owner's agent gets a request to rent residential property in Berkeley from an applicant and the owner charges a fee to purchase a consumer credit report and to validate, review, or otherwise process an application, the owner must provide, either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap permitted under California Civil Code Section 1950.6(b).
rules.requirement: Before charging a screening fee, landlords must provide prospective tenants either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and the maximum fee cap under California Civil Code Section 1950.6(b).
rules.title: Tenant Screening Fee Disclosure Requirements

rules.coverage_text: All residential rental properties in Berkeley.
rules.quote: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner's agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.
rules.requirement: Landlords may not charge existing tenants any non-refundable fee for renewing a tenancy or for related requests such as roommate departure, addition, or replacement.
rules.title: Prohibition on Non-Refundable Fees for Existing Tenants
